landing.heading: Only the book posts.
landing.lead: BookWyrm has no public API, but it federates. Lesesalen reads the outboxes of the BookWyrm accounts you follow, recovers the fields Mastodon throws away, and lays them out as five distinct kinds of card.
landing.principleHeading: You see a post because you follow that account
landing.principle: Your follow list is read in your browser, and the feed is the outboxes of those you follow who are on a BookWyrm instance. Nothing more.
landing.noCrawler: The server never fetches anything on its own initiative: every single request happens because a reader is present and follows that account.
landing.sampleNote: The example below is invented. A stranger arriving here never sees other people's reading.

sections.heading: What this is
paragraphs: Lesesalen is a Mastodon client that shows you the book posts and nothing else. Five kinds of book post, five distinct looks — laid out as a reading room instead of a microblogging timeline.

BookWyrm has no public API, but it federates. The problem is that Mastodon discards the rich fields: the rating, the review title, the quoted passage, how far into the book the reader is, and the link to the book are all custom ActivityPub properties Mastodon has no column for.

sections.heading: Where the posts come from
paragraphs: The feed is the outboxes of the BookWyrm accounts you follow, not your home timeline. Your follow list is read in your browser with your own token; of those accounts we keep the ones on a BookWyrm instance and read their outbox page by page.

The reason is that one outbox page yields fifteen already-complete objects for one request, where the timeline needed one fetch per post. The same work for a fifteenth of the traffic at the instance we are a guest of — and the whole of an account’s reading history, not just what your instance happened to receive.
What is lost is boosts and followers-only posts. A book post boosted by somebody you follow is in nobody’s followed outbox, and a public outbox contains only public posts.

sections.heading: Why there is a server
paragraphs: The origin object is public and addressable. Fetch it with Accept: application/activity+json and you get the whole object back — type, rating, title, quote, position and a link to the edition.

The browser cannot do this itself, because BookWyrm instances send no CORS headers for ActivityPub fetches. That single fact is the entire reason there is a server in this project. It does four things: looks up what software an instance runs, reads a page of the outbox of an account you follow, re-fetches a single origin object, and caches bibliographic data and covers.

sections.heading: What this deliberately is not
paragraphs: You see a post because you follow that account. Same as Mastodon, minus boosts. Nothing more.

So there is no crawler. Lesesalen does not walk the fediverse collecting BookWyrm posts into a database, and there is no background job: the server only fetches while a reader is present. The posts are public, but public is not the same as consenting to be aggregated, indexed and re-served by a third party the author never heard of. A BookWyrm user posting a review to their followers did not sign up to be in somebody’s corpus.
For the same reason there is no logged-out timeline and no discovery surface. A stranger arriving here sees an explainer and some invented samples — not what other people are reading.

The posts we have fetched for you are stored in your browser, so we do not have to fetch everything again each time you come back. They never sit on our server, and if you have ticked the box to be logged out when the tab closes, they are not stored at all.

sections.heading: Replies
paragraphs: You can reply, favourite and boost through the Mastodon API. A post fetched from an outbox has no Mastodon id, so one is looked up at your instance the first time you act on the card. If your instance does not have the post and cannot fetch it, we say so rather than letting the action fail.
A reply becomes an ordinary Mastodon post — not a BookWyrm comment. Mastodon cannot mint BookWyrm objects, and we would rather say that once too often than once too seldom.

sections.heading: Contact
paragraphs: Lesesalen fetches from instances we do not own, and tries to be a polite guest: one request per second per domain, an honest User-Agent, and we respect 429 and Retry-After. Reading the outbox instead of every post separately is part of the same thing — it is fifteen times fewer requests. If something is still a nuisance, get in touch and we will fix it.

privacy.title: Privacy

points.detail: The server has no user table. There is no login on the server side at all.
Your login stays in the browser and goes only to your own instance.

points.term: Your follow list is read in the browser
points.detail: It is never sent as a list. But the feed is the outboxes of the BookWyrm accounts you follow, and to fetch an outbox the server has to be told which account it belongs to. So it does see the addresses of those accounts — one at a time, never how many others you follow, and never the ones that are not on BookWyrm. See the caveat below.

points.term: No reading history on the server
points.detail: Post content passes through memory and is discarded. A restart empties everything, and that is how it should be. What we have fetched for you is stored in your own browser instead — and not even there, if you have ticked the box to be logged out when the tab closes.

points.term: No analytics, no cookies, no third parties
points.detail: No tracking, no CDN, no external scripts or fonts.

kept: Which fediverse instances run BookWyrm. That is infrastructure, not personal information, and one lookup serves everybody.
Bibliographic data and cover images for books that have been seen: title, authors, page count, ISBN and the link to BookWyrm. A book edition is not anyone's personal information.

Covers are downloaded once, when a book is first cached, and then served from here. So your IP never reaches the instance that owns the image, and because the fetch happens at cache time rather than per view, the server learns nothing about who looked at what.
The posts we have fetched for you, in your own browser. Not on our server, and not at all if you have ticked the box to be logged out when the tab closes.
privacy.caveat: The endpoints that fetch from BookWyrm accept two kinds of address: the URI of a post to be shown, and the URI of an account you follow, when its outbox is to be read. So the server does see which posts somebody is reading, and who they follow on BookWyrm. The second is new, and is the price of building the feed from outboxes instead of the timeline; the first was always so, because a post URI contains the account name. Neither is logged, stored, or tied to any identity, and the answers go out no-store. But it is not nothing, and it belongs here rather than being smoothed away.
privacy.rights: There is no export on the server side, because there is nothing there to export. The collection in your browser you can clear at any time under Settings. To remove your login, log out: the token is revoked at your instance first, then cleared from the browser, and the collection goes with it.
